caption: Perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on different validation datasets under varying quantization bits.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The provided image contains three separate bar charts, labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, each illustrating the perplexity of the LLaMA1-7B model across different quantization bit settings on their respective validation datasets. Each chart displays two sets of bars for each quantization bit value: one representing the “Uniform” quantization method (blue bars) and the other representing the “Ours” method (orange bars), as indicated by the legend in each subplot. The horizontal axis, labeled “Quantization Bits,” lists the bit values 3, 4, 8, and 16, presented in ascending order. The vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” is scaled linearly and represents the perplexity score, with the range and tick intervals varying per chart to accommodate the respective data ranges. In chart (a) WikiText, the y-axis spans from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 5. In chart (b) PTB, the y-axis spans from 0 to 400, with tick marks at intervals of 50. In chart (c) C4, the y-axis spans from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The bars are grouped by quantization bit value, with the “Uniform” bar appearing to the left of the “Ours” bar in each group. The height of each bar corresponds to the perplexity value for that method and dataset combination, with specific values labeled on top of each bar. For instance, in chart (a) WikiText, the “Uniform” bar at 3 bits reaches a value of approximately 30, while the “Ours” bar at 3 bits reaches approximately 22. In chart (b) PTB, the “Uniform” bar at 3 bits reaches approximately 400, while the “Ours” bar at 3 bits reaches approximately 250. In chart (c) C4, the “Uniform” bar at 3 bits reaches approximately 30, while the “Ours” bar at 3 bits reaches approximately 21. The bars are not visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or other visual cues beyond their color and height. The charts do not indicate any specific ordering of the bars beyond the sequence of quantization bits along the x-axis.
model_annotations.English: The provided image displays three side-by-side bar charts, labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, each illustrating the perplexity of the LLaMA1-7B model across different quantization bit settings (3, 4, 8, and 16 bits) for two methods: “Uniform” (blue bars) and “Ours” (orange bars). In each chart, the horizontal axis represents “Quantization Bits” and is labeled with the discrete values 3, 4, 8, and 16, while the vertical axis represents “Perplexity” with a linear scale. The y-axis ranges from 0 to a maximum value specific to each chart: 30 for (a) WikiText, 400 for (b) PTB, and 30 for (c) C4, with tick marks at regular intervals (e.g., every 5 for WikiText and C4, every 50 for PTB). In chart (b) PTB, the “Uniform” method shows a much higher perplexity, starting at approximately 400 at 3 bits and decreasing to around 300 at 4 bits, then 300 at 8 bits, and 300 at 16 bits. The “Ours” method shows significantly lower perplexity, approximately 250 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 180 at 4 bits, then 180 at 8 bits, and 180 at 16 bits. In chart (c) C4, the “Uniform” method starts at approximately 30 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 25 at 4 bits, 8 bits, and 16 bits. The “Ours” method shows lower perplexity, approximately 21 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 19 at 4 bits, 8 bits, and 16 bits. The bars are not sorted by value and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color-coding.
